speaker: gerrydonates
text: Okay, thank you. Good morning, Mayor Rodriguez and Vice Mayor, city commissioners and city administration. And I hope everyone is well and their families are safe. And my name is Jerry Donatis. I was the senior manager for the city's audit of the fiscal year ended September 30th, 2019. And I'm just going to provide a brief presentation on the results of the audit. Start things off, the opinion in the audit report was an unmodified opinion. So that's good, it means it's a clean opinion. And there were no new accounting policies that were adopted during the year that had a significant impact on the financial statements. There was a new standard that was implemented, referred to as GASB 88 related to debt disclosure, but that was just a matter of additional disclosures in the notes that didn't have any significant, didn't have any impact on the numbers. In terms of the audit process, we had no difficulties in dealing with management while we completed and performed our audit procedures. And we didn't have any disagreements with management. The finance director, city manager, entire staff, everything we requested, they provided it to us in a timely and efficient manner. In terms of adjustments, there were a few audit adjustments that were posted related to depreciation for the enterprise funds assets and some reclasses of expenditures and capital outlay expenditures. There were no findings in the 2019 audit report, and there were also no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies that were noted in the report. And in addition, there were no prior year findings to address as well. In terms of some of the balances, on an overall overview, in the executive summary that you received, the first page has a four-year comparison of the governmental funds and the enterprise funds. There you'll see the unassigned fund balance in the governmental funds, which is coming from the general fund, has been increasing steadily over the last several years. And this year it increased approximately $250,000. So as of September 30th, 2019, the unassigned fund balance was about $975,000. Now this is good news because in 2010, 2011, that number was only about $50,000. So an increasing over the last nine, 10 years. Now, ideally you want this balance to be about three months of the budgeted expenditures. So that would take you to a range of 1.5, 1.6 million, but it's getting there. It's definitely getting there. As I mentioned, it's remained consistent. It has been increased. It has gone down a year here or there related to the general fund having to subsidize the enterprise funds, water and sewer funds, but the increases have been consistent. And if the city is able to continue that, it will slowly be able to work towards reaching the goal of the unassigned fund balance of about three months worth of expenditures. In the enterprise funds, there were no drastic changes and the issues there have been the same as they have. And the goal there is again, to come up with solutions, to fund the aging water and sewer system and the major improvements that are needed, which will need some significant funding. In terms of revenues and property tax revenues and other tax revenues increased as expected, the red light revenues increased when compared to 2018. And so that was a good sign. And then the FEMA grant funding from Hurricane Irma, that was received in 2019 and the city was able to pay off the line of credit that it had from City National. The second half of the package, you can read on your own. There's a letter there to management and the commission, which basically touches on some of these things I've mentioned. And at the end, there's some financial statements, balance sheets and income statements for the various funds. You can see some more details. And then I basically wanna conclude with just two more comments. In 2019, there was a federal single audit as well, which is related to the fact that the city reported federal grant expenditures of more than $750,000. And the major program that was audited was the FEMA grant related to Hurricane Irma. Now, obviously those expenditures were incurred two or three years before the way these disaster grants work. When the project worksheets are approved and the funding is allocated for the year, that's the expenditures in the schedule. So we, and I know from experience in dealing with these disaster grants, it's a tough undertaking dealing with these grants and it took, you know, look how many years it takes to receive the funding, but so I would like to commend, you know, the city and the finance department for the way it carried it out. We had no findings related to the compliance testing of the grant and the opinion on the single audit was unmodified as well. And then lastly, just wanted to touch on the pandemic. Obviously all businesses and cities are affected by this. And so, you know, we need management and the commission definitely need to evaluate the effects that it is having on the city and will have on the city. So some measures can be, you know, drafted or to mitigate any of the loss of revenues that the city may have, you know, for, I know for a fact the red light camera revenues are going to be decreasing that nobody's been driving around the last couple of months. If certain offices of the city were closed, no revenues were coming in. So that's just something to keep in mind as the rest of the year ends now in 20, and then while you prepare for the 930, 2021 budget. In closing the, you know, I believe the city's management once again has done a great job maintaining the budget and the finances of West Miami. And the challenge continues to be just finding a solution for the improvements and that are needed in the water and sewer system. I'll turn it over to Carlos. He says he'll say a couple of other comments. I mean, questions feel free to ask and whether now or anytime during the year we're always available. Thank you.

text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. Would anyone like to provide a little more information on this item?

speaker: ericdiazpadronvi
text: Yeah, I'll begin. So as the clerk stated, this is a discussion item, so it has not been, the proposal hasn't been written yet. And this came from, it's modeled after a county ordinance from a few years back. Actually, Commissioner Blanas has joined us, I wanted to be part of this discussion. So you can, Madam Clerk, if you didn't recognize him.

speaker: annery
text: Duly noted.

speaker: ericdiazpadronvi
text: Commissioner Blanas, we're just starting now the items. This is a discussion item that was modeled after a county ordinance that from a few years back that was widely supported on the county commission is very popular in the community that allows residents to repair damaged but not destroyed fences after a natural disaster, after a hurricane, without going through a permitting process again. So what it does is it speeds up their ability to fix the fences aesthetically, so it doesn't have, it's not an eyesore for the neighbors, for safety reasons, without going through a permitting process. Obviously, if the fence is destroyed, then they would have to go through the permitting process to build a new fence. It doesn't have to be for all fences, we can limit which fences would apply. That's something I spoke with the manager prior to placing this item, but I would like to bring this up for discussion.

speaker: rhondaar
text: Thank you, Vice Mayor. I'd like to hear from public services on this item as well. Does public services have any input on this item?

speaker: juanpenapublic
text: Yes, I do. Good morning, Mayor, Commissioners, Vice Mayor. The last time when this ordinance was brought up through Miami-Dade County, number one, it was because Miami-Dade County is very vast and their building department was not able to get up and running right away. They did it mostly because of the pool conditions that were left open to the general public. We have a different scenario in the city of West Miami where the most pool backyards here are required to have an easement. For people to go out and try to replace or put up fences where they have not been properly permitted could cause expenses to the homeowner by having to move the fence at a later date. And we have never had the problem with being able to open right after a storm. Usually public services back in service two hours, three hours after the storm has passed. So, and our ability to have a cloud service for a building department allows us to work from anywhere to be able to issue permits or even apply for permits.

It was brought up, but it passed and it's very popular and it works. So, and I understand Mr. Pena's objection, but frankly, if we went with every objection administration I don't think we'd ever get anything passed. So if anyone else has any discussion on that.

speaker: juanpenapublic
text: Well, vice mayor, it really isn't an objection.
